subject: Eiffel Tower
title: What If Someone Sold the Eiffel Tower for Scrap? In 1925 a Con Man Did

scenes.text: What if someone sold the Eiffel Tower for scrap? In 1925, a con man collected the money.
It starts with a newspaper story: the tower is costing Paris a fortune in repairs.
Victor Lustig poses as a government official and invites scrap dealers to a grand hotel. On offer: seven thousand tons of iron.
One dealer bites. By the Smithsonian's account he hands over about seventy thousand dollars, including a bribe.
Lustig vanishes with the cash. The dealer is too embarrassed to tell the police.
So he comes back and tries it again. This time the police hear of it. He flees to America, where counterfeiting lands him in Alcatraz.

description:
What if someone sold the Eiffel Tower for scrap? In 1925 the con man Victor Lustig read that the tower was expensive to maintain, posed as a deputy director of France's Ministry of Posts and Telegraphs, and offered its 7,000 tons of iron to scrap dealers at the Hotel de Crillon.
One dealer, Andre Poisson, paid; Smithsonian Magazine puts the total at about 70,000 dollars including a bribe. Too embarrassed, he never reported it. Lustig returned to try the trick again, then fled to the United States, where he was later jailed for counterfeiting and sent to Alcatraz. He died in 1947.
